_meta.purpose: Print-run authority. This table is what makes a variant claim checkable rather than a judgement call: if a set never printed a variant in a given language, any claim that a card has it is false by construction.
_meta.provenance: Modeled from public collector references. NOT licensed eBay or TCGplayer data. See docs/DOMAIN_PRIMER.md section 3.
_meta.language_scoping: variants_printed is keyed by language because the rule is language-scoped. English sets stopped carrying a 1st Edition stamp with the EX series in 2003; Japanese printings continued much longer.
_meta.reverse_holo: Introduced with Legendary Collection (2002). A reverse-holo claim on an earlier set is impossible.

sets.name: Base Set
sets.note: The only English set that printed shadowless. Print order was 1st Edition Shadowless, then Shadowless Unlimited, then Unlimited with the drop shadow.

sets.name: Jungle
sets.note: No shadowless printing. A shadowless claim here is false by construction.

sets.name: Team Rocket
sets.note: Home of the 'Dark' prefix Pokemon - Dark Dragonite, Dark Charizard.

sets.name: Legendary Collection
sets.note: First English set with reverse holos. No 1st Edition printing.

sets.name: EX FireRed & LeafGreen
sets.note: EX era. English 1st Edition was discontinued before this set - any 1st Edition claim is impossible.

sets.name: SM Black Star Promos
sets.note: Promo series, not a numbered main set. Home of Armored Mewtwo (SM228), tied to the 2019 film.

sets.name: Champion's Path
sets.note: THE DEMO CASE. No English 1st Edition printing exists - the practice ended in 2003. A model asked 'is that 1st edition?' about the 074/073 Charizard VMAX will often say yes, because '1st edition Charizard' is overwhelmingly common in its training data. This row is what blocks it.

sets.name: Celebrations
sets.note: 25th anniversary set. Flying Pikachu V appears here.

sets.name: SWSH Black Star Promos
sets.note: Home of Special Delivery Pikachu (SWSH144), a Pokemon Center exclusive.

observational_attributes._note: These exist only in the physical card in the seller's hand. The copilot must NEVER assert them - it defers to the host. See DECISIONS.md D-12. Observed in the wild repeatedly: 'is the back clean?', 'Swirl?', 'Back again plz'.

nicknames._note: Observed in real chat. Exact-match lookup fails on every one of these, which is why the entity matcher needs a nickname table plus fuzzy matching. Each entry is a live test case.
